answers: The main issue with somatic cell nuclear transfer is related to the reprogramming ability of the enucleated egg cell. When the ovum's nucleus is removed, the cell loses its genetic information, which is believed to affect the special factors in the cytoplasm that are responsible for reprogramming implanted somatic cell nuclei into cells with pluripotent states. This reprogramming ability might be negatively impacted due to the physical linkage of critical embryonic genes to oocyte chromosomes or potential damage caused to the cytoplast during the removal of the egg nucleus or insertion of the somatic nucleus.  Despite many attempts , success in creating human nuclear transfer embryonic stem cells has been limited . There lies a problem in the human cell 's ability to form a blastocyst ; the cells fail to progress past the eight cell stage of development .  Also, questions remain on how homologous the two cell types truly are .

history.content: what is the process of somatic cell nuclear transfer

The process of somatic cell nuclear transfer involves two different cells: a female gamete (also known as an ovum, egg, or oocyte) and a somatic cell, which refers to the cells of the human body such as skin cells, fat cells, or liver cells. First, the nucleus of the donor egg cell is removed and discarded, leaving it 'deprogrammed'. Then, the somatic cell is inserted into the 'empty' ovum. After being inserted into the egg, the somatic cell nucleus is reprogrammed by its host egg cell.

The general story is narrated by an unknown narrator , and in this narration the stories are told by Scheherazade . In most of Scheherazade 's narrations there are also stories narrated , and even in some of these , there are some other stories . This is particularly the case for the `` Sinbad the Sailor '' story narrated by Scheherazade in the One Thousand and One Nights . Within the `` Sinbad the Sailor '' story itself , the protagonist Sinbad the Sailor narrates the stories of his seven voyages to Sinbad the Porter . The device is also used to great effect in stories such as `` The Three Apples '' and `` The Seven Viziers '' . In yet another tale Scheherazade narrates , `` The Fisherman and the Jinni '' , the `` Tale of the Wazir and the Sage Duban '' is narrated within it , and within that there are three more tales narrated .
